text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Government wants to create a holding to concentrate its stakes in pulp and paper companies. The holding would subsequently be privatised.
- Siemens/Mota & Companhia partnership is favourite in the third phase of the competition to build an underground train system in Porto.
- Tobacco company Tabaqueira privatisation may be delayed 45 days after Economy Minister Augusto Mateus decided to consult the country's Competition Council about the likely impact.
- Banco de Comercio & Industria (BCI), which is preparing to leave the bourse, may price stock to be bought back at 1,100 escudos.
- Portuguese Prime Minister Antonio Guterres and Nobel Peace Laureate Jose Ramos-Horta on collision course over financing for East Timor resistance movements.
- National Chemists Association and Health Ministry clash over the payment period for state financed medicines.
- Forestry industry may grow 42.8 percent by 2000, according to Alberto Mesquita former chairman for the European Confederation of Wood Industries.
- Banco Totta & Acores (BTA) privatisation last phase starts today.
- Health Minister Maria de Belem backs former minister Leonor Beleza in controversy over plasma contaminated with AIDS.
- Petrol company Petrogal posted 5.5 billion escudo profit in the first three quarters of 1997. By the end of the year Petrogal will become shareholder in gas distributor Trangas.
- Portugal's largest trade union group CGTP says companies owe 9.3 billion escudos to more than 8,000 employees in back-pay.
